items.title: We Build LEGO Godzilla, Who Will Tower Over Your Other LEGO Models
items.content_text: For Black Friday 2026 , LEGO is launching a massive model of Godzilla, King of the Monsters. It is a LEGO Ideas model, which means it began its life as a fan design by Matthew Esposito . He received the requisite votes for official LEGO approval, and he will also share in the profits. This is a bulky build that looks more impressive in person than it does on its box cover. It comes with two interchangeable mouth insertions: either a large tongue or an Atomic Heat Ray, the latter of which extends his height to over two feet tall. Space concerns aside, the choice seems clear if you're putting this city stomper on display. Godzilla fans should know this model is based upon the ongoing ' Monsterverse ' iteration of the creature, which began with Godzilla (2014). Monsterverse is an American franchise, not to be confused with the original Japanese Toho franchise, which released its 34th film ( Godzilla Minus Zero ) this November. But artists have redesigned Godzilla many times, including from movie to movie. So even though it might not be the exact Godzilla you love the most, this LEGO model is immediately recognizable as the icon, because it has the general characteristics that most iterations share in common: the pear-shaped body, the comparatively smaller dinosaur head, and the dorsal fins that line its back. The model's main inspiration is the Godzilla from Godzilla: King of the Monsters (2019), but even so, it's a bit sleeker and thinner than that one. So it might be best to think about this as yet another monster design alongside the others – loyal to the design ethos, but unique in its approach. LEGO Godzilla comes in a large box, which encases two smaller boxes. Each smaller box contains approximately 20 bags. Added together, it's 41 bags in all, plus three instruction booklets. There are no stickers and no printed tiles. You build one leg, then the pelvis, and then the other leg. You connect both legs to the pelvis with durable ball joints, and stand it up. To give you an idea of how bottom-heavy Godzilla is: Just the legs and pelvis comprise half of the entire build. And even so, LEGO made clever design choices to accentuate his bulk. Take the armor plating on his lower legs, for example. They hang off a hinge near the ankle, which creates the illusion of a thicker, more substantial leg, even though it's mostly air with no bricks to fill it out. Then you focus on the tail, which you build in segments. Connecting them all creates a sense of accomplishment, because most large LEGO builds (including this one) take shape through layering, first by building the Technic skeleton underneath and then building the musculature and skin via plating. But with the tail, you're seeing the entire appendage take form in front of you, immediately, and it's easy to see where it begins and where it will eventually end. Each tail segment contains dorsal fin elements. You need to either build directly onto the tail piece or clip a larger fin to it, which adds a varied, visual touch. The tail drags along the ground, and the instructions let you decide whether it will rest on the left side or the right side of the creature. You then turn to the correct page (sort of like a Choose-Your-Own-Adventure book) and proceed. The third and final instruction booklet shows you how to build the arms, the head, and some final, large dorsal fins on the creature's back. These are the fussiest parts of the build, owing to their smaller size and weaker connection points. But when everything is complete, the final result is very intimidating. Ironically, the smaller head and arms only emphasize how large the rest of the creature is. Godzilla's skin cleverly appropriates the LEGO bricks' pips as rough texture. This is a wonderful model, and we recommend it with one important reservation; it is best displayed from a side profile angle only, with its head pointed upwards. Any other angle or posture, and the model looks odd and ungainly. I think the reason for this one-dimensionality – for favoring one possible display angle over the others – is the developers were trying to nail a single, iconic Godzilla pose. It's this one from the promotional poster for Godzilla: King of the Monsters, in which Godzilla is looking up, shooting his atomic heat ray directly towards the heavens: And to be fair, this model nails that pose very, very well, and it looks exactly like the poster. But that comes at the sacrifice of other possible poses. Take the neck, for example. To ensure that the head can tilt up convincingly, the designers included extra grey bricks around the neck to hide the seams. That's a great thing, but only for that specific pose. Those extra bricks limit Godzilla's movement, and he can only point his head up, diagonally up, or straight across. He can't, for example, look down, which is a problem if you want to pose him looking down at the city or humans he's about to destroy. It's not a problem isolated to the neck either; the back is also ramrod straight and does not allow Godzilla to adjust himself down or forward. Again, that's fantastic for that one pose . But it doesn't serve Godzilla well for any other, alternative setup. Normally, this sort of one-notedness, especially in adult sets, wouldn't be that big of a deal, because an adult set doesn't need to be a malleable plaything. But because so much of our popular concept of Godzilla has him looking down at things rather than up at them, it's especially noticeable. Surely, a creative builder can modify the current set for more flexibility. And then, LEGO Godzilla can look down as he stomps some LEGO Ninjago cities, while minifigures scream and scramble for dear life. LEGO Godzilla (Set #21375) retails for $449.99 and includes 5363 pieces. It will be available beginning on Black Friday, November 27.
items.title_en: We Build LEGO Godzilla, Who Will Tower Over Your Other LEGO Models

items.title: Rockstar Explains Why it Added Consequences to GTA 6's Violence and Crimes
items.excerpt: Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson has explained why the studio added the divisive criminal profile system to GTA 6.
items.content_text: Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson has explained why the studio added the divisive criminal profile system to GTA 6 . In an interview with Eurogamer , Nelson was asked about Rockstar's approach to the systems and themes in GTA 6. He said that a lot of it was born out of all of the work they put into Red Dead Redemption 2, specifically having a reactive world that responds to the player's behavior and choices. He explained that there was a desire to evolve the GTA experience and to "give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun.'" That means players can now point a gun at someone and threaten them, rather than having to beat or kill them to steal their money. The threat of violence is just as prevalent as the violence itself in GTA 6, and it also plays into the morality-adjacent system that is your criminal profile. The game doesn't explicitly punish you for doing bad things, because it's GTA, and you're bound to do bad things. However, it judges you on how harsh you are. If you rob a store with minimal force or only attack people if they draw on you first, attempting to minimize casualties, your profile won't change. If you go in and kill everyone, the level may decrease. This prompted Rockstar to expand NPC interactions even further. If you drew a gun in GTA 5, no one cared until it was actively pointed at them. Now, people will begin to quietly scurry away if they see you pull a rifle out of your trunk. Nelson explained that while the powerful rampages were fun for a while in previous games, they lacked substance and would get old quickly. In GTA 6, the process to start mowing people down takes a bit more thought because you don't have an endless pocket of weapons anymore. "You have to call your car," says Nelson. "You have to pop a car trunk and get [a weapon], and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable. And then they're still fleeing in terror, but then there's people who also have guns, and they're shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up, and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them. "And then, you choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off, and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!' And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your criminal profile until it breaks, and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'" The more realistic approach with GTA 6 has been a bit divisive for purists. Some don't want consequences; they want a power fantasy, and GTA 6 is decidely not that. If you want a supercar, it's going to take you dozens of hours before you can steal one. There's a progression to the chaos. For some, that's more rewarding. For others who want that quick fix, it's cumbersome. It'll be interesting to see how Rockstar looks at all of the responses to the game and how that informs the next GTA. Will they go further down this path or will they try to find a greater middle ground? The game certainly isn't hurting despite some vocal critics. GTA 6 is the highest rated game in history on Metacritic and generated nearly $4 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours , making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. IGN gave the game a 10 out of 10 , praising it for its depth and detail. "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, GTA 6 has not stopped astonishing me since I started it," reads an excerpt from our review. "I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."
items.title_en: Rockstar Explains Why it Added Consequences to GTA 6's Violence and Crimes

items.title: Spotify Reveals Massive Spike in Streams for Music Featured in GTA 6
items.excerpt: Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6, including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago.
items.content_text: Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6 , including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago. In an email sent to IGN, Spotify revealed that the GTA 6 hype is inspiring listeners to add tons of music from the game to their playlists. In addition to hype for the original music created specifically for the game, such as Justice's Flower in a Hurricane, Carly Rae Jepsen's 2015 song Run Away With Me saw a 940% increase in streams following the game's release. The song plays during a pivotal moment in GTA 6's first chapter and is arguably one of the best sections in the game. Additionally, fans are listening to the official GTA 6 playlist en masse and are actively searching for things related to the game. You can view the full breakdown courtesy of Spotify below. Following the release of GTA 6, streams of Carly Rae Jepsen's “Run Away With Me” spiked on Nov. 24, increasing by 940% in the U.S. and 1,255% in Canada compared to its average streams. On Nov. 23, “Flower In A Hurricane” by Justice, Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard hit number 1 on BOTH Spotify’s Daily Top Songs charts globally and in the U.S. Streams of The Official Grand Theft Auto Playlist surged week over week, rising 275% globally and 355% in the U.S. (on Nov. 19 as compared to Nov. 12). GTA had fans searching for more. Searches containing “GTA,” “GTA6/VI” or “Grand Theft Auto” surged about 510% globally and 600% in the U.S. compared with the week prior (Nov. 19 vs. Nov. 12). GTA 6 has been shattering all kinds of records and setting new trends. The game had the biggest launch in the history of PlayStation and sold nearly $4 billion worth of copies in its first 24 hours , making it the highest-grossing entertainment launch of all time by a significant margin. The game has also set viewership records on platforms like Twitch , led to a massive increase in internet traffic , and so much more. It's a massive cultural moment that's likely not going to end anytime soon. Not only will this game likely get bigger, but it also has more big events on the horizon. It's also expected to release on PC early next year, and an online mode is also heavily speculated to come in the future. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? items.title: The Lord of the Rings Illustrated Editions Are on Sale for Black Friday
items.content_text: Amazon's popular '3 for 2' deal on books , vinyl, and more is back for Black Friday , with some great inclusions to pick from. In the books section, you can save on both versions of The Lord of the Rings illustrated edition, two versions of The Hobbit illustrated edition, as well as The Illustrated World of Tolkien: The Second Age. These printings of J.R.R. Tolkien's fantasy epics are rather large compared to other books, but make for beautiful display pieces or good gifts for any Lord of the Rings fan . Buy 2, Get 1 Free Lord of the Rings Books The illustrated versions of the Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit are no stranger to getting the Black Friday treatment (or any other sale), but they're always one of the most popular items for a reason. Each one is a beautifully bound collection of the iconic stories we've grown to love over the decades, but with illustrations, notes, maps, and paintings from J.R.R. Tolkien himself. The Hobbit illustrated by Jemima Catlin is another great addition to the collection, thanks to her unique art style and depiction of the characters. Which special edition should you buy? Both special edition hardcovers of The Lord of the Rings include the same illustrations but with different levels of quality. As you can imagine, the Deluxe Illustrated Edition is quite a bit more expensive, but includes a more expensive looking cover and slipcase. It also has overall thicker pages than the regular special edition. If you want the ultimate experience, it's worth upgrading to the Deluxe Edition. Otherwise the regular special edition is just fine. You should also consider that Amazon's 3 for 2 sale is only as good as the least expensive item you buy, so opting for the $100+ version won't necessarily save you any more money here. And if you've been keeping up with Prime Video's The Rings of Power series (check out our review of the season 3 finale ), The Illustrated World of Tolkien: The Second Age depicts events that happen throughout the show. It's a hardcover retelling events of the 3,500-year period before The Hobbit by David Day, and makes for a good source material companion while watching the show. items.title: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Reveals That Every Hunger Games Movie Has Initially Been Rated R
items.excerpt: Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he has directed in the series were initially rated R and opened up about the process of making them PG-13.
items.content_text: Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he directed in the series were initially rated R, prompting clever workarounds when editing them. On paper, The Hunger Games franchise is tonally very interesting. Although it's a young adult novel series, targeting teenagers, it's about children being forced to fight to the death in a dystopian society. The books don't hold back on the violence, and the films have always had to walk a fine line so they can reach the widest audience possible. The process of making the movies PG-13 is complicated and often inconsistent. When speaking with Kevin McCarthy , director Francis Lawrence noted that all five of the Hunger Games films he has worked on were initially rated R. The director noted that across his whole career, he has run into an issue of making a movie with a PG-13 rating in mind, but the MPA (Motion Picture Association) reserves the right to give it an R if it's too "intense," even if there's no excessive blood, gore, language, or nudity. It happened with Constantine, it was a concern with I Am Legend, and it has happened regularly with The Hunger Games series. In one of the Mockingjay films, Lawrence had to cut a scene of a little girl crying and screaming over the body of her dead mother. There wasn't any blood, but the performance was so visceral that it pushed the film closer to an R-rating. He revealed that the process is somewhat subjective, as the people who rate the movies change, their tastes change, and he was even able to identify specific changes on particular movies. In regards to Sunrise on the Reaping, he believes that the MPA has become more "conservative" with their judgment of a film, prompting them to tweak the project and show it to the organization four or five times. He also said that sometimes he makes the content more intense on purpose when presenting it to the MPA, so when they edit it, they can show the "intended" version, and it looks more tame by comparison. One example of this is amplifying sound effects to make it sound gnarlier, and then reigning it in on subsequent edits. Lawrence went on to note that he is surprised by how much these movies can get away with in a PG-13 context, but believes there's a thematic relevance that the MPA accepts. "It does help that there's been so many of these now that there's [a] precedent," he said. "There's also real thematic relevance to these stories, and I think that also really helps, that in the end they're anti-violence stories. They're about the consequences of violence, the consequences of war; they're really about themes that are educating people. I do think the MPA takes that into consideration when they look at sequences that are intense. They have different emotional values, and it's not really splattercore, in a way. "But I definitely do intensify beyond a limit of where I think it will be accepted as PG-13 purposely, because I know we are going to have to pull back on certain things." He explained that certain deaths were more brutal and gratuitous in initial cuts of the film, but ultimately had to be adjusted for a PG-13 rating. "One thing I really wanted to keep was we had a very specific neck wound on Maysilee in her death. Basically the one that kills her is right here," said Lawrence while pointing at the center of his neck. "And he's covering it and when his hand comes off, you can see blood starting to drip out of it, and you can see the hole, and it's why she can't speak. And they made us get rid of that, and that's what killed me." The Hunger Games films are far from the only big mainstream action movies that have to get creative with how they depict violence. Crew members on The Dark Knight were confident the film would be rated R, despite Christopher Nolan and the studio working to avoid that. They were able to get around a harder rating thanks to the fact the film does most of the gorier acts of violence off-screen or even playing it off as a joke. "It’s kind of shocking that The Dark Knight ended up being PG-13," said the film's cinematographer Wally Pfister in a 2018 interview . "All of Chris’s movies would be PG-13 to open it up to a wider audience. Somehow, he always had some magic with the MPA. "Lo and behold, he has the pencil and I’m like, 'You are not getting the PG-13 with that. There’s no way this is going in. He’s driving this pencil through a guy’s head!' And I was wrong. Chris was always right, whether you liked it or not. You’d be like, 'F*** you, you were right again.' With this pencil trick, I thought, ‘If it has the right amount of levity, we’ll sell this and it won’t come off as being violent but it’ll come off as being a magic trick and it’ll come off as being a punchline.’ And it was!" Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now.

items.title: Rings of Power Showrunner Explains the ‘Different Side’ of Simon Pegg’s Balrog: It ‘Actually Is True to the Books’
items.excerpt: The Rings of Power Season 3 is full of creatures and bigger canon references, from Simon Pegg's Balrog to the Fell Beasts, Oliphaunts, Great Eagles and more.
items.content_text: Spoilers follow for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 1-8. The third season of Prime Video’s The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has come to a close, strengthening its ties to author J.R.R. Tolkien's mythology, creatures and iconography, and even explicitly leaning into the design and execution of creatures and places seen in Peter Jackson’s film adaptation. If you’re not a canon expert a la Stephen Colbert, or haven’t re-watched the films recently, below is an explainer on many of the creatures featured in Season 3, with insight into how they connect to the books or the films. More From Middle-earth The Rings of Power Season 3 Finale Recap and Review Rings of Power Stars React to Those Big Season 3 Deaths Where the Rings Are at the Start of Rings of Power Season 3 The Rushed Rings of Power Episode Release Schedule Explained Breaking Down Theo's Shock Moment in Rings of Power Season 3 The Balrogs: Intelligent Super-Beings Balrogs were servants of Morgoth, the Dark Lord, during the First Age. After his fall from power, many Balrogs were wiped out in battle, but a few survived. In The Rings of Power narrative, at least one lived deep inside the Misty Mountains, and it was awakened by the dwarves mining for Mithril. In "Orodruin,” Sauron seeks out that particular Balrog (voiced by Simon Pegg) to gain its knowledge about safely using the Flame of Udûn to forge the One Ring. In return, Sauron promises to free the creature and give it Khazad-dûm to rule. Co-showrunner Patrick McKay told IGN that Tolkien’s text describing the Balrog influenced how they interpreted the fire beast. “One of the things that's cool in the books is if you really look into the lore that Tolkien built for his entire life, the Balrogs are intelligent super-beings,” McKay explained. “They aren't just monsters. They're cunning and they are battlefield commanders in the First Age. It opened up the possibility that we could show you a different side of him. Maybe one you're not expecting, but one that actually is true to the books and the conception.” McKay and Episode 7 director Stefan Schwartz described the scene in the Misty Mountains as a dramatic “negotiation” between the Balrog and Sauron. “The scene goes from [Balrog’s] total disdain to actually being won over by Sauron to actually helping him in his quest to create this ring,” Schwartz pointed out. 'They aren't just monsters. They're cunning and they are battlefield commanders in the First Age.' McKay said casting director Theo Park came up with the idea of asking Simon Pegg to voice the Balrog opposite Charlie Vickers’ Sauron. “Simon Pegg is often known as a comedic actor because of the earliest films he did with Edgar Wright, but he can kind of do anything,” McKay said. “This was an opportunity to do something he hadn't done before, and he took to it like a duck to water.” Schwartz confirmed that Pegg was on set, performing live into a microphone to Vickers, who was looking at a light box which represented the Balrog’s placement in the frame. “They could rehearse it and run the lines and then actually play it, and then we could talk about the nuance of how he is brought over to Sauron's way of thinking,” he said. An ally of Sauron’s by the end of Season 3, the Balrog’s rule over King Thrain (Eddie Marsan) and the dwarves will play out in Season 4 (and 5 if it gets a greenlight). The Fell Beasts: Sauron’s Dark Ride In the opening minutes of Episode 4, "Gundabad," Sauron is introduced to his future steed — an extremely ornery beast that is resistant to the bridle. In Tolkien’s letters, the author described them as winged, stinking creatures with no feathers, just bare skin. The author also referred to them as fell beasts, as well as Nazgûl-birds, which makes sense because in the book version of The Return of the King, fell beasts become the replacement steeds for the Ringwraiths. However in The Rings of Power, Sauron expounds on their origins more specifically, telling the orcs, “They were once eagles, you know. Until Morgoth blessed them with his touch. Taught them to crave his lash, to survive on only the foulest of meats.” Because of that, Sauron knows the way to tame one is through feeding it living flesh, which he does by feeding it random orcs. The steady meals allow Sauron to bridle the beast, which he first uses to chase Galadriel to Mount Gundabad and then the forests of Greenwood. By the end of the season, Sauron has taught Nazgnagôl Theo ( Tyroe Muhafidin ), and likely the others, how to ride a fell beast. He uses it to dive-bomb the Númenórean army and freak out their soldiers on the eve of battle. Look for them to return when the real war between Sauron and Middle-earth begins in a future season. The Great Eagle: Saving Our Heroes (Again) In the last minutes of "Gundabad," before Galadriel, Arondir, Celeborn and Marnûkh are trapped by Sauron and Nazgnagôl Theo on a ledge in Mount Gundabad, Galadriel releases a flaming arrow into the sky like a rescue flare. It spurs a snow-covered Giant Eagle in the mountain to awaken and fly into action. Galadriel instantly recognizes it is Landroval, Prince of Eagles. He gets hit by an orc arrow but survives to save Galadriel and Celeborn from falling to their deaths. Landroval is a heroic figure across Tolkien’s ages. In The Hobbit, the eagle will save Thorin and company from the burning trees. And at the end of The Return of the King, Landroval is one of the three Great Eagles who rescue Frodo Baggins and Samwise Gamgee from Mordor after they destroy the One Ring. The Oliphaunts: The Gandalf Connection The elephant-like creatures found south of Mordor are called oliphaunts in Tolkien’s text, and are formally introduced in The Rings of Power in Episode 3, "The Secret Fire.” Gandalf comes upon one in battle armor under the Dark Magic control of Pallando (Ciarán Hinds). Despite getting thrown around by the aggravated beast, Gandalf frees the creature from its constraints in an act of kindness. In "The Lady of Lórien," Gandalf tries to turn Pallando away from Sauron but gets knocked out by the Dark Wizard and is instead bound and strung up to ride prone, on top of an oliphaunt, as he’s taken to Sauron. In Peter Jackson’s The Two Towers, oliphaunts are visually established in live-action battles, though they are entirely CGI creations. Showrunners Patrick McKay and J. D. Payne decided to carry through that take on the creature into The Rings of Power for continuity. Gandalf’s Hat: An Origin Story In Episode 3, "The Secret Fire,” Gandalf has a vision when he visits the Secret Fire and realizes his mission is to redeem Pallando, not conquer him. When he returns to Tom Bombadil’s cottage, his friend is gone and all that’s left is his signature hat. Gandalf takes it as his own, completing the iconic silhouette — long beard, staff and hat — that’s synonymous with the wizard. In the finale, "The Doom of Men,” Gandalf crosses paths with Tom once again on his long journey back to the elves. His wizarding mentor tells him to keep the hat, cementing its new ownership with his blessing. What creatures or references did you pick up on in Rings of Power Season 3? Let’s discuss in the comments!

items.title: GTA 6 Animation Director Reveals Rockstar Made 3 Animations for Each Item Interaction
items.excerpt: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.
items.content_text: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game. If you’ve been playing GTA 6 at all, you’ve probably picked up on the fact that characters can now hold an item in each hand. This has made for some especially funny clips on social media, where users have wasted no time making Jason recreate the ‘six-seven’ meme while holding various objects. This is a big change from previous Rockstar games; in titles like GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 , players could only carry one thing at a time, though you could dual wield certain guns in GTA: San Andreas. (You could also hold longarms at your side while shooting a pistol in RDR 2 and Max Payne 3 .) Now, you can hold a sandwich in one hand and a drink in the other — or a bag and a gun, if you’re sticking up a pawn shop, for instance. This isn’t just an aesthetic feature, either, as it serves the important function of letting players take care of two tasks at once, making robberies or transporting items a bit smoother. Players have praised GTA 6 for its jaw-dropping attention to detail, and this particular tidbit wasn’t lost on them. A thread on Bluesky discussing the feature caught the attention of Mike Jones, the director of gameplay on Rockstar’s latest title, who revealed the extent of the studio’s efforts in making sure every single item interaction had a single-handed, two-handed, and hands-free animations. “FYI, we made three versions for all item interactions; one if both hands are free, one if just your right hand is free and again for the left,” he wrote . “It was a massive pain, but once you knew every interaction could ‘cope,’ it made the game logic much easier. That was then sometimes replicated for crouch, too…” That being said, the devs at Rockstar aren’t superheroes, and they had to cut corners somewhere during development. Jones admitted this fact in response to another comment in this thread, where a user wrote, “Honestly, the level of polish is so absurd that when I see how cheated the ‘putting gas in the car’ sequence is, I'm like, relieved. ‘Oh, okay, they're human, they bleed.’ You all did SO well.” “Thanks, everyone would really appreciate your comments! And yes, shortcuts were definitely made, too,” Jones replied. GTA 6 is a game like no other. Its world is so massive and detailed that some players are avoiding progressing the story in favor of chilling out in Key Lento and diving for treasure, fishing with Cal, and playing billiards at the Rusty Anchor. And we can’t blame them; there’s tons of stuff to do, even in Chapter 1. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . items.title: LEGO Announces 4 New Sets Based on the Harry Potter HBO Series
items.content_text: The LEGO Harry Potter theme has been a mainstay since the first set came out in 2001. Now that HBO has a new TV adaptation of the Wizarding World in the works (set to debut on December 25), LEGO has finally unveiled a new batch of sets based on the new series. Four new sets have been announced, two of which are available to preorder now. They're all out January 1. Let’s take a look. Featured in this article The four sets offer a nice selection of characters and locations from the first book, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone, which is what the HBO show’s first season adapts. Honestly, these sets don’t look all that distinct from the sets based on the movies. Then again, based on the TV show’s trailer , they didn’t really change much when adapting the franchise into a show. LEGO Harry Potter: Privet Drive Preorder at LEGO It all starts on 4 Privet Drive. That’s where we find the home of the Dursley family, who adopt Harry Potter after you-know-who kills his parents. The Dursleys aren’t very nice to Harry, but this LEGO set lets you build their two-story house, complete with Harry’s cupboard under the stairs. This one’s available for preorder now. LEGO Harry Potter: Gryffindor Common Room Preorder at LEGO The three main young wizards all end up in house Gryffindor, so they spend a lot of time in the common room. This set recreates that cozy space, complete with a fireplace, five minifigures, and a Quidditch table that’s unique to the show. items.title: 'People Are Doing It Too Quickly Now' — The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Speaks Out on YA Franchise Reboots
items.excerpt: I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted.
items.content_text: I got the chance to sit down with the director of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Francis Lawrence, who opened up about the amount of remakes happening in Hollywood and how he would feel if The Hunger Games series ever got rebooted. Francis Lawrence has directed all but one movie in The Hunger Games series. He’s been with the franchise for over a decade; the first film, directed by Gary Ross, released in 2012, after which Lawrence took up the mantle for all subsequent movies. It’s one of several iconic movie franchises that defined the YA boom of the 2000s - mid-2010s. And unlike other series from this time period, it has neither languished nor suffered a reboot before its corpse is even cold. HBO’s forthcoming Harry Potter series is perhaps the most egregious example of such a reboot. The last Harry Potter movie released in 2011, and its cast defined an entire generation of fans who grew up watching their adventures at Hogwarts. It seems almost insulting to reimagine the world that was so painstakingly built over the course of a decade — but that’s just my opinion. I’m not alone in this line of thinking, though. When asked about his feelings on reboots, Lawrence agreed that they’re happening too soon, bringing up Warner Bros.’ thankfully canceled idea for an I Am Legend reboot in 2014, just seven years after the original film was released. “I mean, I do feel like people are doing it sort of too quickly now,” he mused. “I agree with you on that. People started talking about that with I Am Legend. I don't remember how long ago, but it felt like 10 years had gone by or something, and somebody was thinking of remaking it already at Warner. I'm like, ‘Really? 10 years, that's it?’” Given the imminent release of HBO’s Harry Potter series on Christmas day, I had to bring up the very real possibility that The Hunger Games sees a reboot in the next decade or so — an idea that Lawrence wasn’t sure would get Suzanne Collins’ blessing. “I don't know how I would feel about it,” he admitted. “I also don't know if Suzanne has anything in place to sort of protect against that, but that'd be really, really interesting to figure out. But I think it's a tough one. I mean, if Suzanne backed it, I think some spinoffs, and obviously if she writes other books, things like that could be interesting, as long as she backs it and comes up with it and has the thematic reasonings and philosophies that she usually does, that would be cool. But I don't know how you go back and remake the original movies and it not be [Jennifer Lawrence]." To his point, The Hunger Games franchise has managed to stay in the public consciousness, owing in part to its later release during the YA boom (the final film in the original series came out in 2015) and its two prequel movies that rocked theaters in the 2020s. The latest movie, Sunrise on the Reaping , received solid reviews from critics, earning an 8 out of 10 from IGN. For more news on this newest entry in The Hunger Games series, check out my interview with star Joseph Zada , who told me all about how he managed to pull off Woody Harrelson's unmistakable accent, and whether or not the cast is Team Peeta or Team Gale .
